It holds up. `n` is the length of the list, so every line gets the same value. `reindex` wants the position of the line, which is the loop index.

There is a second one on line 50, and you did not mark it. `append` sets `dirty = true` but never reindexes, and only `rebuild` clears that flag.

input.text: append sets dirty = true but never reindexes, and only rebuild clears the flag. A line added after a rebuild keeps a stale index until the next one.

It is on the diff now. `]c` jumps to it, `d` deletes it if you disagree.

This is the sharper of the two. It is silent, and it only bites when a read lands between the append and the next rebuild.
